name: Stock V15 (M-VAVE)
author: M-VAVE
why: The factory firmware. 6-op DX7-style FM, 128 presets, ARP and 16-step SEQ. The baseline every mod is measured against and the required starting point (V15) before flashing anything else.
features: 12 voices, 32 algorithms, 6 FX, arp, 16-step seq, DX7 SysEx bank import, CC 0-23 on FX channel. Receives clock/start/stop since V13; never sends clock.
sounds: 128 factory voices in 4 banks (A-D), DX7 .syx bank import, 6 FX
midi: IN: USB, BLE, TRS. OUT: notes only (USB/BLE). Clock in since V13, no clock out. CC 0-23 on FX channel

name: FM1 Open Firmware (fm1_open)
author: M-VAVE
why: M-VAVE's own short-lived open-source release of the firmware and SDK (board drivers, audio HAL, WASM workbench). Pulled offline, but its leak of HAL code accelerated the whole scene.
features: 8 tracks, 8 sample slots, build.bat for pi32v2 Clang and WASI SDK, web workbench.

name: Felucca
author: Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton)
why: The root of the family tree. First complete open replacement OS: 13 engines, 4 tracks, 64-step sequencer, web editor, build guide. Nearly every other firmware forks this.
features: ANALOG, DIGITAL 4-op FM, PHASE, LOFI, SAMPLE, VOICE, TRIO, WHEEL, GRAIN, FM6, PHYS, SLICE, NOISE. 4 tracks / 8 voices, slicer, mod matrix, USB audio, MIDI LEARN, per-track channels. midi_clock.c handles 24 PPQN + Start/Stop.
emulates: Original multi-engine groovebox (OP-Z / Dirtywave M8 spirit)
engines: 13: ANALOG (2 osc VA), DIGITAL (4-op FM), PHASE (Casio PD), LOFI (chiptune), SAMPLE, VOICE (formant), TRIO (3 osc), WHEEL (tonewheel organ), GRAIN, FM6 (DX7), PHYS, SLICE, NOISE
sounds: Factory presets per engine, GM drum track, user sample slots, DX7 .syx import
sequencer: 4 tracks / 8 voices, 64 steps, chords, ties, slides, live rec, per-track slicer
midi: IN: USB + TRS, per-track channel, MIDI LEARN. OUT: USB. Clock in 24 PPQN + Start/Stop. USB audio out

name: Felucca [Salt]
author: Chance Roth (ChanceTheMaker)
why: Felucca with the MIDI polish the base lacked: TRS input with full expression, selectable clock source, on-device MIDI monitor, 20 palettes, and a browser Studio that plays without hardware.
features: GLO > GLOBAL > CLK = INT/USB/TRS. Ch 1-3 synth parts, ch 10 drums. Pitch bend, modwheel vibrato, sustain, panic. Favorites, Terminus fonts, LOWCUT speaker filter.
sounds: 54 presets in Studio, Felucca factory sounds, favorites
midi: IN: USB + TRS with sustain, bend, modwheel, panic. Clock INT/USB/TRS + Start/Stop/Continue. On-device MIDI monitor. OUT: USB

name: Melodee
author: Kerem Kilic (keremimo)
why: Felucca rebuilt around classic polysynths: a real Prophet-5 Rev4 model with all 200 factory programs, a Casio CZ-1 engine, SID, and microtonal FM6. For people who want a vintage synth, not a groovebox.
features: PROPHET, FM6, CZ-1, SID, DRUM engines. 70 tunings, .syx import/export, 32 pattern banks, unified note editor, QNT. Ships fm1-recover tool. Author wrote the clock PR used by Salt.
emulates: Sequential Prophet-5 Rev4, Casio CZ-1, Commodore SID, Yamaha DX7
engines: PROPHET (2 osc, SSI/Curtis filters, poly-mod), CZ-1 phase distortion, SID, FM6, DRUM
sounds: 200 Prophet-5 factory programs, 64 CZ-1 factory tones, 64 DX7 slots, 70 microtonal tunings, .syx import/export
sequencer: 4 tracks, 32 pattern banks, 1024 notes, note editor, QNT
midi: IN: USB + TRS, ch 1-4 tracks, ch 10 drums. Clock INT/USB/TRS + Start/Stop/Continue. OUT: USB notes. SysEx preset import

name: ChoralRoot FM-1
author: Quixotic7
why: Ports the Monome-grid ChoralRoot chord engine: one hand picks roots, the other shapes voicings. Exists for chord-based live performance rather than step sequencing.
features: Two-handed chord shaping, custom key modes, bass line, looper, color UI, browser emulator. Community remix adds Prophet-5 + Morph + BASS engine.
sounds: Felucca presets; remix adds Prophet-5 (200) + BASS engine

name: X0X
author: Charles Vestal
why: A ReBirth RB-338 in your pocket: 909, 808, two 303s with acid generators and a breakbeat player, all at once. Built because the FM-1's form factor begged for a drum-machine box.
features: 16 patterns, song mode, knob automation, reverb + tape delay sends, master compressor/filter/limiter. Manual + web emulator.
emulates: Propellerhead ReBirth RB-338: Roland TR-909, TR-808, 2x TB-303

name: GHOULBOX 2.0
author: Jason Persinger
why: A genre firmware: dungeon synth and dark ambient. Cathedral HALL reverb, worn-cassette tape stage, a hurdy-gurdy engine, historical temperaments, RPG-styled UI.
features: GURDY engine with crank clicks, drone latching, 36+ crypt/choir/lute/organ sounds, skull boot screen, full browser emulation before flashing.
engines: Felucca engines + GURDY hurdy-gurdy, HALL reverb, TAPE/CRKL
sounds: 36+ dungeon sounds: crypt pads, monk choirs, lutes, organs; historical/just temperaments

name: Jangada
author: zednaked
why: Dark, industrial, Brazilian-accented take on Felucca with ratchets, drone modes and custom kits. Exists as a personal sound-design flavor of the platform.
features: 10 engines incl. 6-op FM and superwave, 4 tracks, mod matrix, ratchets, evolving drones, custom drum kits, web Studio.

name: REDACTED
author: DJ Redacted
why: Experimental fractured lo-fi box with performance macros FRACTURE / STATIC / CHANCE / MUTATE on the top knobs. A vibe firmware with a broken-vinyl splash screen.
features: Four layers PULSE, VOLTAGE, STATIC, GHOST chosen via ALGORITHM; real-time track shapers.

name: Hortator
author: DEADACTIVE
why: A dedicated drum machine. 808/909 and Mutable Plaits drum models, Grids generative rhythms, user samples, pumping compressor. Fills the gap for people who want the FM-1 as a drum brain next to other synths.
features: 8 tracks, Grids pattern generator, LFOs, live FX, acoustic resonators. Drum channel set in GLO > CH; Bluetooth variant build.
emulates: Roland TR-808/909 + Mutable Instruments Plaits drums + Grids
engines: 808/909 models, Plaits drum models, user samples, resonators
sequencer: 8 drum tracks, Grids generative patterns, fills, LFOs
midi: IN: USB, TRS, BLE. Clock in all three + Start/Stop. Drum channel in GLO

name: April OS
author: beashoko
why: Sampling first: 32 sample slots, slice and loop editor, record straight from a phone or laptop mic. Exists because stock has no sampling at all.
features: 32 slots x 3 s, 8-track sequencer, slice/loop editor, direct audio recording via browser.
sounds: 32 user sample slots x 3 s, record from phone/laptop mic

name: WaveLoop FM-1
author: ELI7VH
why: Felucca tuned for being driven by an Arturia MiniLab 3: faders to tracks, encoders follow track, DJ filter, punch-in FX pads. Exists for external-controller performance.
features: Track fader mappings, follow-the-track encoders, DJ filter mode, momentary FX pads, class-compliant USB MIDI out, vibrato.
emulates: Felucca driven by an Arturia MiniLab 3
midi: IN: USB + TRS, MiniLab 3 fader/encoder map. Clock INT/USB/TRS. OUT: USB

name: Rainbow mode
author: joshbartlettband-web
why: A children's instrument: rainbow color-coded keys, 40 animal sounds, safe volume limiter, with the full Felucca hidden behind a secret key combo.
features: Color keys, animal SFX and rhythms, volume limiter, hidden Felucca.
sounds: 40 animal sounds and rhythms, hidden full Felucca

name: fm1-chord
author: math0ne
why: Chord composition tool, chord sequencer, rhythm accompanist and ear trainer. Exists as a songwriting and practice aid rather than a performance box.
features: Chord sequencing, accompaniment, ear training, MIDI in and out.

name: DUELL
author: OSCILL/R (balinthcom)
why: Two full independent parts (LAYER / SPLIT / STEREO) with patch morphing between two states. Exists for multitimbral keyboard playing, something stock cannot do.
features: Per-part engine, arp, EQ, mod matrix, sidechain duck, ping-pong delay. Per-part MIDI channel, program change, bank select. Tested on one unit so far.
emulates: Bi-timbral performance synth (Roland JV / Korg layer-split era)
midi: Per-part channel, program change, bank select, clock sync, CC for morph. Sidechain duck via MIDI

name: MAKU (幕間機)
author: okumurari2
why: Always-on generative ambience for DJ intermissions: power on and an in-key evolving soundscape is already playing. Buttons are verbs that nudge the world; REC saves worlds you like.
features: Pulse/Floor/Haze/Voice parts, new scale and tempo every boot, taste memory (16 likes), CC20 kick density.
midi: IN: USB + TRS, clock follow, CC20 kick density

name: Polly
author: Charles Vestal
why: A Yamaha QY70 in your pocket: 8-track arranger with chord recognition, styles, fills, intro/outro and QY style import on a General MIDI engine. Exists for songwriters who want a backing band.
features: Drums, perc, bass, 5 chord tracks via Sonivox EAS GM, chord follower from keys or MIDI IN, WASM simulator.
sounds: Full GM bank, accompaniment styles, QY style import
sequencer: 8 arranger tracks, chord follower, fills, intro/outro
midi: USB in; GM via MIDI IN

name: TRIBE
author: Alexandre Piel (apiel)
why: X0X taken further: 10 freely assignable tracks, 25 engines, 16 clips per track, scatter FX from zicBox. Exists for Elektron-style clip-based live techno.
features: KICK W/P models, 909/808, 303, 16 clips/track, 6 clock rates, 4 directions, scatter FX, dual master FX, compressor, WASM emulator.
sequencer: 10 tracks, 16 clips each, 16-64 steps, 6 rates, 4 directions

name: Golana
author: Gadlele
why: Recreates the Korg microKORG workflow and MATRIX editing, with live waveform and filter-curve drawing on screen. Exists for people who want one deep virtual-analog synth.
features: 4 voices, 2 osc, dual LFO, patch matrix, 24/12 dB LPF, BPF, HPF, MS-20 style filter, 16-step seq, arp, FX chain.
engines: 4-voice VA, 2 osc, dual LFO, patch matrix, 24/12 dB LPF, BPF, HPF, MS-20 LPF

name: FANTASMA / Pelucco
author: Gadlele
why: Haunted generative ambient with Omnichord strum mode and very long AMBI reverb. Also introduced a built-in USB Rescue Boot (hold OCT- at power-on) so a bad flash is recoverable.
features: 3-channel self-generating music, BELL drifting loops, Pads/Lead/Bells/Noise roles, OMNI strum, ECTO theme, rescue boot as FM-1_000.
sounds: Pads, lead, bells, sea/wind noise roles

name: Skiff
author: illuminus5
why: Felucca with more tracks and an Elektron-style sequencer: p-locks, microtiming, ratchets, trig conditions. Exists for deep step-sequencing.
features: 6 tracks, 14 engines (VA, FM, wavetable, physical, drums, noise), 64 steps, p-locks, probability, send FX, mod matrix, web editor.
engines: 14: VA, FM, wavetable, physical, drums, noise
sequencer: 6 tracks, 64 steps, p-locks, microtiming, ratchets, trig conditions

name: Felucca 8 Patterns
author: echoe
why: Felucca 1.5.1 with 8 chainable patterns per track for song arrangement, paid for by dropping sample playback to free flash. Exists for arranging full songs.
features: 8 pattern slots per track, chaining, no sample engine.

name: SLOOP
author: isod89
why: The second big platform. A live groovebox for any style with no mandatory presets: 3 synth tracks + drums, 64 steps, song mode, USB audio in, web editor with backup/restore. Most mature and most forked after Felucca.
features: 12 engines incl. 6-op FM with DX7 import, 153 sounds, 37 kits, user samples, p-locks, microtiming, fills, swing, 27 punch-in FX, DUST/DUCK/FILT master. GLO > SYSTEM > SYNC. OUT = SEQ sends sequencer notes.
emulates: Teenage Engineering OP-Z / Elektron live groovebox
engines: 12: analog, FM, 6-op FM w/ DX7 import, physical, noise, drums
sounds: 153 sounds, 37 drum kits, user samples, user presets
sequencer: 4 tracks (3 synth + drums), 64 steps, p-locks, microtiming, fills, swing, song A-D
midi: IN: USB + TRS. Clock USB/TRS + Start/Continue/Stop, clock-only mode. OUT: sequencer notes (OUT=SEQ). USB audio in

name: sloopDX
author: Sven Trogus (zvenson)
why: SLOOP workflow plus a sample-identical Dexed msfa DX7 engine, a resonant filter behind every voice, and a programmable 16x8 FM drum machine. For DX7 purists who still want a groovebox.
features: 256 .syx voices in 8 banks, CUT/RESO filter, on-device operator editing, 5 FM drum kits with macros, OMNI chord harp, 128 steps/track.
engines: Dexed msfa 6-op FM (32 alg) + resonant LPF, FM drums
sounds: 256 .syx voices (8 banks), 20 modern patches, 5 FM kits x 16 sounds

name: FM1 Move
author: Nicodesy06
why: Ableton Move workflow on the FM-1: 8 tracks, clips and scenes instead of a linear song arranger, custom 240x240 UI. Hardware verification still in progress.
features: 8 tracks any synth/kit, clip and scene launcher, web simulator, device page for backup/presets/samples.

name: FM1 Quest
author: hericdk
why: SLOOP as a fantasy sidescroller: tracks are party heroes, steps are attacks, BPM is walk speed, recording triggers boss fights. Exists for fun.
features: Game UI over the SLOOP core, web emulator.

name: JIANT FM
author: juanjiant-bit
why: Thermal-camera themed 6-track OS where each engine behaves like an organism. Adds bytebeat/floatbeat LOFI with 32 formulas and a mix-bus slicer.
features: T1-T6, 8 songs x 4 sections, ANALOG/FM6/PHASE/LOFI/VOICE/WHEEL/NOISE/DRUM-X, SL BUS slicer, visualizers, web editor and emulator.
engines: 8: ANALOG, FM6, PHASE, LOFI bytebeat, VOICE, WHEEL, NOISE, DRUM-X
sequencer: 6 tracks, 8 songs x 4 sections, SL BUS slicer

name: ORBIT
author: dspaudio
why: SLOOP with Teenage Engineering OP-1 visuals, sample tools and an event tape for shifting what tracks play. Exists for the OP-1 aesthetic.
features: Sample manipulation, event tape mechanism, 4 tracks, web emulator.

name: NoteSorcery
author: catacombius
why: OP-1 style 8 tracks with live USB sampling and project export straight into Ableton Live sets, plus an Android controller app. Exists to bridge the FM-1 into a DAW workflow.
features: USB audio sampling, Ableton .als export, Android companion.

name: SLOOP ALG
author: shaw-core
why: Experimental fork adding Karplus-Strong strings, plucked models, additive synthesis, DX7 and VA to SLOOP.
features: New engines on the SLOOP core, companion editor.

name: FM80S
author: Floydus
why: Synthwave-oriented synth-looper for stacking loops into songs, with planned 8-track expansion.
features: Live loop stacking, step seq, song assembly.

name: SLOOP DX7 Banks
author: majnikool
why: SLOOP with 12 categorized DX7 banks (384 voices) in flash for instant preset browsing without touching your project.
features: Keys/Bass/Leads/Pads/Strings/Brass/Perc/FX categories, fast navigation.

name: SLOOP Floyd FM
author: René Bohne
why: Adds Floyd Steinberg's 4-operator FM algorithms and a live scope/envelope display to SLOOP.
features: 4-op FM with custom matrices, on-device oscilloscope and ADSR view.

name: SLICE64-FM
author: jeymadcat-ops
why: Beat-slicing box: 64 slices across keys with transient detection, reverse and per-slice pitch, plus FM accompaniment.
features: Auto transient detection, slice reversal, per-slice pitch, FM synth.

name: winampFM
author: hericdk
why: SLOOP 2.6 dressed as Winamp 2.x: playlist preset browser, EQ-slider FX, tape looper, 28 pixel-art visualizers, Brazilian instruments. Exists for nostalgia and party performance.
features: 157 sounds, reel-to-reel looper with auto BPM, PARTY mode, 3D web simulator.
sounds: 157 sounds incl. cavaquinho, berimbau, agogô, sanfona, Brasil kits
sequencer: SLOOP + tape looper w/ auto BPM, PARTY mode

name: FoMni-1
author: Charles Vestal
why: A Suzuki Omnichord: strum white keys like a harp plate, pick chord root and type on black keys, with rhythm accompaniment. Exists for non-keyboardists.
features: Strumplate, chord selection, accompaniment and arp modes.

name: FuMi-1
author: cartesive
why: FoMni fork recreating the Suikohsha ST-50 Japanese Shigin accompaniment instrument with koto, sho, shakuhachi and taiko in historical just intonation.
features: Traditional voices, ST-50 scale system, web emulator.
sounds: Koto, sho, shakuhachi, taiko in ST-50 just intonation

name: Baud Girl FM-1+VA
author: Madeline (Baud Girl)
why: Keeps the stock FM engine and your presets but fixes the ergonomics, adds Virtual Analog (7-osc Super mode, ZDF filters), an 8-bit engine and a 64-step sequencer. The only free firmware documented with MIDI Clock Out.
features: FM + VA + 8-bit engines, 64-step seq, Sync on ARP/SEQ pages, Clock Out, excellent MIDI/SysEx guide, pattern writes over SysEx.
engines: Stock 6-op FM, VA with ZDF filters, 8-bit engine with drums/game sounds
sounds: Your stock presets kept, VA presets, 8-bit drums
sequencer: 64 steps, dot-matrix seq, Sync on ARP/SEQ pages
midi: IN: USB, BLE, TRS. Clock in AND Clock Out setting. SysEx pattern writes. Full MIDI guide

name: Groove OS
author: Groove OS
why: Paid polished groovebox: up to 8 tracks with independent loop lengths, 6-op FM + VA ladder-filter engines, 20 voices, p-locks, stage view. Exists as the turnkey commercial option.
features: Per-track MIDI out channel, clock in and out, DX7 SysEx reception, curated packs, web emulator.
engines: 6-op FM (12 voices) + VA w/ ladder filter (8 voices)
sequencer: 8 tracks, loop lengths 1-8 bars, 64 steps, p-locks, stage view
midi: Per-track MIDI out channel, clock in + out

name: Bubba Machine
author: Erbubar23
why: Written from scratch in C99 with zero third-party audio code, every kit procedurally synthesized. TR drum machine, 8-slice sampler, wavetable bass, polymeter per track. Hardware flasher still on the roadmap.
features: T1 TR drums, T2 Sampler 3.0, T3 wavetable bass, T4-6 assignable incl. MIDI, 4 scenes, 16 punch FX, crash-safe flash.
emulates: TR drum machine + MPC-style sampler, written from scratch
engines: TR drums (procedural), 8-slice sampler, wavetable bass, synth/mono/kit/MIDI tracks
sounds: All kits and wavetables synthesized in C, take library
sequencer: 6 tracks, polymeter 1-64 steps, clock mult/div, 4 scenes, 16 punch FX
midi: Internal clock only (so far); MIDI track type planned

name: zp12
author: Sven Trogus (zvenson)
why: An authentic 80s 12-bit drum sampler (SP-12 / Linn spirit): 26 kHz, rate-skipping pitch with no interpolation, 8 cut channels with decaying filters, MPC swing. Drop your own WAVs from the browser.
features: 32 pads / 4 banks, 11 loops on black keys, 4 songs, 4 punch FX, browser sample dropper.
engines: 12-bit 26 kHz sample playback, rate-skip pitch, 8 channels w/ resonant filters
sounds: 32 pads x 4 banks, drop your own WAVs from the browser
sequencer: 11 loops, 4 songs, 16-step grid, MPC swing 50-71%, 4 punch FX

name: FiMba-1
author: J. Adam Sowers
why: A thumb piano: detailed kalimba/mbira physical model at 44.1 kHz with tine, resonator and buzzer parameters, traditional tine layout, mbira pattern generator.
features: Tine or chromatic layouts, granular cloud FX, WASM emulator with preset saving.
engines: Physical model 44.1 kHz: tines, resonators, buzzers; granular cloud FX

name: Lunar Modulator
author: ip2k
why: Brings Mutable Instruments engines (Plaits-style models, 160+) and a Movy-style sequencer with p-locks to the FM-1. Still browser-only, not flashable yet.
features: 5 engines, 4 FX, step sequencer with parameter locks, virtual FM-1.

name: AMB-1
author: Charles Vestal
why: Music for Airports in a box: unsynced tape loops of unequal lengths, gliding bass, Euclidean percussion, playing from power-on.
features: Self-generating, tape-loop model, web emulator and manual.

name: CTL-1
author: Charles Vestal
why: Turns the FM-1 into a MIDI master controller: keys send notes, knobs send CC in four banks, TRS passed through, with GM sounds for monitoring. Exists so the FM-1 can drive your other synths.
features: Multi-channel USB/TRS controller, 4 CC banks, internal GM monitoring.
midi: OUT: keys as notes, knobs as CC in 4 banks, multi-channel, USB + TRS passthrough

name: PurpleMonkey FM-1
author: Quixotic7
why: Zero-menu toddler toy: 5-note pentatonic scale and backing beats.
features: Pentatonic keys, drum beats, web emulator.

name: FM-1 B-Boy Edition
author: friendsmakenoise-prog
why: Late-90s hip-hop chop sampler: 3 sample tracks plus an FM bass/lead lane.
features: Sample chopping, FM lane.

name: fm1-polyseq
author: NOVALENTI
why: A strict-C99 bare-metal HAL for the AC791N with a polyphonic 16-step sequencer. Exists as a clean-room developer foundation.
features: HAL, 16-step poly seq.

name: FM-106
author: PattF
why: A Roland Juno-106 (KR-106 engine port): 6 voices on both cores, oscilloscope split screen, .syx patch import, USB audio out. Exists for one classic polysynth done well.
features: 6-voice DCO, 4 banks, web Librarian, patch naming, USB-C audio.
sounds: 2 factory + 2 user banks, Juno .syx import via web Librarian

name: ETCH
author: SikkenWorks
why: Draw single-cycle waves on the device, morph between them, modulate with a third. 8 voices, motion recording, generative RIFF arp.
features: Waves A/B/C, wave library, motion rec, arp.
engines: Drawn single-cycle waves A/B morph + C modulator, 8 voices
sequencer: Motion rec, arp with RIFF mode

name: AMBII
author: MilkBoyG / JalopyMusic
why: Alternative performance and recording interface on Melodee's engine core, with automation graphs and undo. Browser prototype, no hardware image yet.
features: 4 tracks, ratchets, automation with undo, Galaxy / Dark Matter themes.

name: MC-1
author: dspaudio
why: Roland D-50 Linear Arithmetic synthesis (PCM attack + synthesized sustain) in an MC-303 style 4-track groovebox with TR drums and 303 acid.
features: LA engine, Drums/Bass/Chords/Lead lanes, web companion.
engines: LA synthesis (PCM attack + synth sustain), TR drums, 303 acid

name: OberVave
author: Sven Trogus (zvenson)
why: An 8-voice Oberheim OB-Xa / OB-8 style polysynth: dual osc, sync, cross-mod, morphing 12/24 dB filter, voice drift, unison. One classic American poly.
features: 8 voices, SEM/Curtis filter morph, dual LFO, chorus/delay, on-screen filter curves.
engines: 8-voice VA, 2 osc, sync, X-mod, SEM/Curtis morphing filter, drift, unison

name: fm1-rocket-os
author: cmlarsen
why: Ableton-style clip launcher and matrix sequencer forked from X0X.
features: Clip matrix (WIP).

name: Optimist
author: w0ts
why: Pick your own engines, kits, FX and sequencer features at compile time to fit flash/RAM budgets. SLOOP 2.4 project compatible. Exists because 1 MB flash forces trade-offs.
features: make builder, 13 engines to choose, SLOOP-style layers, web librarian.
engines: Pick from 13 engines at compile time

name: Dinghy
author: Sven Trogus (zvenson)
why: Minimal clean starting point for developers: 4-voice sine synth over working display, audio DMA, buttons and USB-MIDI. Start here to write your own firmware.
features: Display, audio DMA, input, USB MIDI drivers, Makefile.

name: Modular-1
author: morgulbrut (wiggismodular)
why: Patch a modular synth in the browser and upload it to the FM-1, with a Euclidean generative arpeggiator. Exists for modular-minded sound design.
features: Visual patch editor, module mod matrix, Euclidean arp.
sounds: Your own patches from the browser editor

name: Hexagon Console
author: unknown
why: Teased hexagonal-UI performance console. Nothing released yet.

name: FM-1 Doom
author: Sven Trogus (zvenson)
why: Because it runs Doom. FreeDM arena map on the 240x240 screen, keys and knobs as controls, keeps sloopDX projects intact.
features: doomgeneric port, HUD, automap.

name: FM-1 NES
author: Keitark
why: NES emulator and, more usefully, a worked example of writing bare-metal FM-1 firmware and app-only updates that preserve the bootloader.
features: 27 keys as controller, APP_UPDATES.md developer guide, no audio.

name: Mocky
author: Charles Vestal
why: Push arbitrary bitmaps to the screen over WebMIDI. A UI mockup and display testing tool for firmware developers.
features: Bitmap over SysEx.

name: fm1-mdx
author: Keitark
why: Sharp X68000 MDX chiptune player with YM2151 emulation, part muting and live accompaniment. Research project.
features: YM2151 software emulation.

name: GameDude
author: Chance The Maker
why: Drop a .gb ROM in the browser, get a flashable firmware. Peanut-GB core on the FM-1 and SMK-37.
features: Web ROM compiler, simulator, palettes.

name: Fart Machine One
author: adamcharleswilsonmusic-code
why: A joke firmware: 11 pitched flatulence samples, 16-step sequencer, delay and reverb. Proof the toolchain is easy enough for jokes.
features: 11 samples, 16 steps, FX.

name: FM-1 Firmware Patcher
author: Christian Zietz (czietz)
why: Keeps stock but fixes the detune calculation to match a real DX7 and disables aftertouch (which caused heavy vibrato from many controllers). Recolors the UI so you know it is patched.
features: python patch_firmware.py FM-1.fwsc FM-1-fixed.fwsc, flash with any updater.

name: FM-1 Macropad Patch
author: smememe
why: Turns stock into a 55-input USB-MIDI macro pad: every button, key and knob sends a note, LEDs off. For desktop hotkey software.
features: Browser or Python patcher.
midi: OUT: every key/button/knob as USB-MIDI notes
